fields.before: 这是只把b的借阅者号换成新号码的方案。借阅履历表中记录着借阅者号，因此一旦重新编号，迁移前的履历里留下的旧借阅者号与迁移后记录的新借阅者号，就无法在表上判别它们指的是同一个人。这违背了「直接沿用现有文件」这一前提。即使把借阅者卡换成内置RFID的新卡，卡上记录的借阅者号本身也应沿用现有的，这才是正确的做法。
fields.after: 这是只把b的借阅者号换成新号码的方案。但借阅履历表是用借阅者号记录「谁借的」，因此一旦重新编号，迁移前的履历里留下的旧借阅者号与迁移后记录的新借阅者号，就无法在表上判别它们指的是同一个人。这违背了「直接沿用现有文件」这一前提。即使把借阅者卡换成内置RFID的新卡，卡上记录的借阅者号本身也应沿用现有的，这才是正确的做法。

fields.before: This option replaces only the user number in b with a new number. The lending history table records the user number, so if the numbers are reassigned, it becomes impossible to tell from the table that the old user number left in the pre-migration history and the new user number recorded after the migration refer to the same person. This goes against the premise of using the current file as-is. Even when user cards are switched to new cards with built-in RFID, the correct approach is to carry over the current user number itself as the number recorded on the card.
fields.after: This option replaces only the user number in b with a new number. However, the lending history table records “who borrowed” by user number, so if the numbers are reassigned, it becomes impossible to tell from the table that the old user number left in the pre-migration history and the new user number recorded after the migration refer to the same person. This goes against the premise of using the current file as-is. Even when user cards are switched to new cards with built-in RFID, the correct approach is to carry over the current user number itself as the number recorded on the card.

fields.before: 如果迁移后仍直接使用既有的文件（表），那么作为其键的号码体系（书籍的识别号、借阅者号）就不要变更。一旦变更代码体系，过去数据与新数据就对不上，迁移的成本和风险都会暴涨。
fields.after: 如果迁移后仍直接使用既有的文件（表），那么作为其键的号码体系（书籍的识别号、借阅者号）就不要变更。一旦变更号码，过去数据与新数据就对不上，迁移的成本和风险都会暴涨。

fields.before: If an existing file (table) is to be used as-is after migration, the numbering scheme that serves as its key (book identification numbers and user numbers) is not changed. If the code scheme is changed, past data and new data can no longer be matched up, and migration cost and risk rise sharply.

If the numbers are changed, past data and new data can no longer be matched up, and migration cost and risk rise sharply.
